Git is like google docs/drop box/track changes 
* Git watches repositories - folders/directories - for changes 
* asks that you describe changes when they're made 
* remembers old versions when you need them 
* looks for conflicts, forces you to resolve them 
* allows multiple people to contribute to the same repository, and does all of the above for everyone at once 

GitHub 
* Git lives on your computer; GitHub is a web-based platform for storing repositories (eg. DropBox but with Git in your folders) 
* GitHub is a great platform for disseminating work. You can easily create and host reports, websites, R packages 
* R projects can initialize Git with a mouse click 

Git client 
* Git is a command-line tool 
* Git clients let you do most Git-related stuff in a GUI - Git client is to Git as R Studio is to R 

Workflow 
* When starting new project: 
  * Create GH repo 
  * created linked R project using repo URL 
  * Do stuff 
  * Once you do stuff, you commit to the changes (commit = save)
  * Git keeps track of changes between commits 
  * Your commit messages will summarize what's different 
  * Once you do lots of stuff, you push changes to GitHub 
  * Branch/merge repos 
  * cloning/forking repos 
  
Pros 
* revert to earlier commits if you mess something up 
* can reveiew development process 
* see what collaborators are doing and why 
* you're forced to resovle conflicts 

Cons 
* lot of overhead 
* resolving conflicts sucks 
* everyone on a project is required to stick with same development pipeline 

Reminder: you can't put confidential data on GitHub - it is public!!!
